question: A team wants Claude to brainstorm names for a new product from the perspective of a branding specialist, aiming for tone and instincts consistent with that professional background throughout the session. What is a simple, effective way to set this up?
options: A) Set a role in the system prompt describing Claude as a branding specialist
B) Ask Claude to name the product with absolutely no role framing given at all
C) Repeat the word 'creative' many times instead of describing any actual role
D) Provide the branding background only in the very last sentence
correct_answers: A) Set a role in the system prompt describing Claude as a branding specialist
explanations: Correct. Setting a role in the system prompt, even a single descriptive sentence, focuses Claude's behavior and tone for the use case, which fits framing a brainstorming session around a branding specialist perspective.
Incorrect. Skipping role framing leaves the tone and instincts of the response to chance rather than steering them toward a branding specialist perspective.
Incorrect. Repeating a vague adjective does not establish the professional framing or tone the team wants for the brainstorming session.
Incorrect. Burying the role description at the end of a long message is a weaker way to establish framing than setting it clearly, such as in the system prompt.
